sources.news_title: Employee kills 2, injures 1 at Virginia rental facility before killing himself
sources.text:
Legal
Employee kills 2, injures 1 at Virginia rental facility before killing himself
An employee opened fire at an equipment rental facility in Manassas, Virginia, killing two people and injuring a third, according to police. The gunman later died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after a police pursuit on Interstate 81.
Police began receiving calls about an active shooter at 7:11 a.m. on Wednesday at United Rentals at 9415 Wellington Road in Manassas. A Prince William County Sheriff’s Office deputy arrived first, followed shortly by Manassas City Police officers.
Police identified the gunman as Marvin Grant, 37, of Charlotte, North Carolina. Manassas Police Chief Douglas Keen said he arrived at work and told a coworker that “three people are going to die.”
Keen said there was an altercation before the employee pulled a pistol from his waistband and shot three people. He fled in a silver Toyota Camry before officers arrived.
Responding officers secured the complex and provided emergency medical aid to the victims, who were taken to hospitals. Ricky Lamot, 48, and Christopher Serrano, 33, later died.
The third victim remains in stable condition at Fairfax Hospital and will need surgery but is expected to survive, Chief Keen said.
Detectives tracked the gunman’s cellphone to Harrisonburg and alerted Virginia State Police. At about 8:20 a.m., state police were notified that he could be in Rockingham County.
A trooper spotted his vehicle traveling south on Interstate 81 near mile marker 235 in Augusta County. He pulled into a rest area near mile marker 232, where troopers attempted a traffic stop.
The suspect got out of the car, then returned to it and continued south, with troopers pursuing him. Near mile marker 227, he stopped along the interstate and stepped out with a firearm pointed at his head.
A tactical team and a negotiator responded. At about 10:30 a.m., he shot himself and was taken to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Virginia State Police said they did not use force.
The motive remains unknown. Keen described the gunman as a relatively new employee, but said investigators were still determining when he was assigned to the facility and whether he had transferred from another location.
Keen also said the suspect changed the vehicle’s license plates sometime between midnight and the shooting. Investigators are trying to determine why.

sources.news_title: 2 killed, 1 hurt in Virginia workplace shooting; suspect also dead, police say
sources.text:
Two men are dead and another is in critical condition after their co-worker opened fire on them at a business in Manassas, Virginia, police say.
The suspect, 37-year-old Marvin Grant, went to work Wednesday morning at United Rentals at 9415 Wellington Road and told a co-worker that three people were going to die, Manassas City Police Chief Douglas Keen said.
“There was some kind of altercation this morning,” Keen said. “He then pulled a pistol from his waistband and shot the three victims.”
The victims were rushed in critical condition to a hospital, where two of them died of their injuries later in the morning. Police identified the victims who died as Richard Lamont, 48, and Christopher Serrano, 33.
An online fundraiser for Serrano’s family says he was a devoted partner and father to a 10-year-old boy and 3-year-old girl.
Keen said he personally knew Lamont, a father who coached youth football in Fauquier County for years.
“September’s been a rough month. We lost a 16-year-old. Now I lost somebody I actually coached youth football with. And knowing what his commitment was and knowing his children and now fatherless, it hits home. It hits home for our community,” Keen said, referring to a shooting earlier this month that killed a 16-year-old girl in Manassas.

Troopers tried to stop Grant after his car pulled into the rest area at the 232-mile marker, police said. Grant got out of the car, but then got back in and kept driving southbound on I-81, according to state police.

sources.news_title: Two people dead, plus suspect, in Manassas, Va., shooting
Manhunt: Manassas Shooting Suspect Marvin Grant Flees
sources.text:
Police in Manassas, Virginia are hunting a United Rentals employee who allegedly shot three coworkers Wednesday morning and fled the scene in a Toyota.
A manhunt is underway for 37-year-old Marvin Grant after three fellow employees were critically wounded at a workplace shooting in Manassas, Virginia. Law enforcement says the gunfire erupted Wednesday morning around 7:00 a.m., and the suspect fled before officers could take him into custody.
Breitbart News reported that Grant worked at United Rentals alongside the three victims, who remain unnamed and were listed in critical condition after the attack.
Manassas City Police identified Grant as the suspect and released a physical description to the public. Officials described him as a light-skinned Black man about 5’9” with brown eyes and brown hair.
Manassas City Police Chief Douglas said investigators believe an altercation preceded the shooting. Officers also believe a handgun was used in the attack.
No full motive has been stated beyond that reported belief about a prior clash. Police have not publicly detailed what sparked the dispute or how quickly it turned violent.
After the shots, Grant left the area. Authorities say he fled in a Toyota carrying a temporary tag from North Carolina. Full year, model, color, and plate details beyond that description were not released in the initial reporting.
A law enforcement speaker identified as Keen addressed the manhunt status directly.
Keen said:
"We know he’s fled the area. We don’t know where he’s headed to."
That admission frames the urgency. Three workers are critically hurt. The alleged shooter is at large. And police cannot yet say which direction he took after leaving Manassas.
WTOP placed the shooting around 7:00 a.m. Wednesday. NBC Washington carried the law-enforcement description of Grant that police put out for the public. Local agencies are treating the case as an active search for a man accused of turning a workplace dispute into a gun attack on coworkers.
No arrest, charges, or recovery of the weapon was reported in the initial account. Victim names and updated medical conditions beyond “critically wounded” were also not released.
Workplace shootings leave families waiting on hospital news and coworkers left to replay what went wrong before the first shot. In Manassas, the immediate task is simpler and harder at once: find Marvin Grant before he can disappear farther from the scene.
When a handgun enters a job-site fight and three people end up fighting for their lives, the public interest is plain. Capture the suspect. Secure the evidence. And hold the person who pulled the trigger to account under the law.

Suspect Kills Himself After Virginia Workplace Shooting
sources.text:
A shooting at a Virginia equipment rental business left two employees dead and a third in the hospital on Wednesday. Police in Manassas say the workplace violence broke out around 7:30am at a United Rentals facility about 30 miles from Washington, DC, ABC News reports. The suspected shooter, United Rentals employee Marvin Grant, fled the scene and killed himself hours later after a standoff with police near Verona, Virginia, around 125 miles southwest of Manassas, CBS 19 reports. Virginia State Police said the 37-year-old died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound following a police chase on Interstate 81.
                                    
                                    
                                
                                
                             
                            
                            
                            
                            
                            
                                
                                
                                    
                                        Police said a negotiator was called in after Grant pulled over around the 227-mile marker and got out of his vehicle with a gun. The standoff lasted around an hour before Grant shot himself, NBC Washington reports. Police said no troopers fired their weapons. 
 -  Manassas City Police Chief Douglas Keen said the shooting happened in a garage area of the business, with numerous other employees present. Keen said there was "some kind of altercation" and Grant "pulled a pistol from his waistband and shot the three victims," ABC reports. He said the motive is unclear, but Grant allegedly said "three people are going to die."
-  Keen identified the slain men as 33-year-old Christopher Serrano and 48-year-old Ricky Lamot, 48, a man the chief knew personally. "The man was dedicated to coaching youth football," Keen said. "Knowing his children are now fatherless, it hits home." The chief said the third victim is in stable condition.
-  This story has been updated with new developments.

sources.news_title: Virginia police searching for workplace shooting suspect driving car with NC tags
sources.text:
Virginia United Rentals shooting: Workers identified in murder-suicide, police say
Virginia law enforcement's search for a man suspected of being in connection to a workplace shooting Wednesday morning with North Carolina ties shot and killed himself.
Get the latest news stories of interest by clicking here.
According to the Manassas City Police Department, officers responded to an active shooter around 7 a.m. in the 9400 block of Wellington Road at the United Rentals facility. The response prompted a temporary shelter-in-place for residents in the area, as well as a temporary lockdown for Dean Elementary School.
Keep up with the latest news and weather by downloading the WXII app here.
"The investigation revealed that this was an active shooter," said Police Chief Doug Keen during the Wednesday morning news conference, "but a workplace violence type call."
Three victims were found by responding law enforcement and taken by emergency personnel to nearby hospitals. Officers said two victims, identified as Ricky Lamont and Christopher Serrano, died from their injuries. All three victims worked for United Rentals.
According to Keen, the suspect -- Marvin Grant, 37, of Charlotte -- fled the scene in a gray Toyota sedan with North Carolina plates. Officers said Grant also worked for United Rentals.
After being spotted by Virginia State Police at a rest stop on Interstate 81 in Augusta County, Grant fled in his vehicle. During an encounter with the Virginia State Police tactical team and a negotiator around 10:30 a.m., officers said Grant pointed a firearm at his head and suffered from a self-inflicting gunshot wound. Officers said he died at a nearby hospital.
"Our condolences go out to the victims and their families. This is a traumatic incident that has impacted many within our community," officers said in a statement on social media. "We’d like to thank our partners with the Prince William Sheriff’s Office, Virginia State Police, Manassas Park Police, Prince William County Police, and Manassas City Fire and Rescue for their assistance with this incident. We’d also like to thank the community for their patience while we conduct our investigation.
Officers said the motive behind the shooting remained unclear and the investigation is ongoing.

Who is Marvin Grant? Manhunt underway for Manassas shooting suspect as 3 injured, schools alerted
Manassas police are investigating a suspect in a triple shooting at a United Rental facility where three victims are in critical condition.
Police in Manassas are conducting an investigation to locate an individual implicated in a triple shooting incident that occurred at a United Rental facility situated in the 9400 block of Wellington Road on Wednesday morning.
According to statements from law enforcement, the suspect in question is considered to pose a significant threat to public safety.
Manassas shooting suspect: 3 victims remain critical
Following the shooting, which took place at approximately 7 a.m., all three victims were transported to local medical facilities where they remain in critical condition, as per Manassas City Police Chief Douglas Keen during an official press conference.
Investigators have determined that the suspect discharged a firearm at three colleagues at the facility following an apparent disagreement. According to reports, two individuals sustained gunshot wounds in the garage section, whereas a third person was shot while exiting an office.

Who is Marvin Grant?
The suspect, identified by law enforcement as Marvin Grant, is described as approximately 5 feet 9 inches in height with brown eyes and brown hair.
“At this point, we do not believe the suspect, Mr. Grant is in the area,” Keen said. “We believe he has fled out of the Northern Virginia area.”
Detectives suspect that Grant may currently be operating a gray Toyota Camry or Toyota Corolla displaying temporary North Carolina registration plates.
A photograph of Grant was distributed by law enforcement authorities shortly before 11 a.m.
Manassas City Schools alerted
Manassas City Schools has instructed all students and personnel at Jennie Dean Elementary School to relocate to Metz Middle School on Wednesday morning, where they shall remain indefinitely due to the closure of Wellington Road.

sources.news_title: Search underway for gunman after 3 shot in Manassas – WTOP News
sources.text:
A man killed himself after police say he fatally shot two of his colleagues and wounded a third during a workplace shooting Wednesday morning in Manassas, Virginia.
Marvin Grant, 37, identified by police as the suspect in the Manassas shooting, was pulled over by state troopers on Interstate 81 in Augusta County, more than a 100 miles away from the shooting scene. Police said Grant shot himself after wounding multiple fellow employees at the United Rentals facility at 9415 Wellington Road.
“Grant came to work this morning, made a statement to a coworker that three people are going to die,” Manassas Police Chief Doug Keen said Wednesday afternoon. “He then produced a handgun and began shooting. What we don’t know is a motive, that brings no relief to our victims’ families.”
In an update Wednesday afternoon, police said two of the employees died and a third was in stable condition following what Keen described as a workplace violence incident. Manassas police identified the deceased men as Richard Lamot, 48, and Christopher Serrano, 33.
According to Virginia State Police, troopers believed Grant may be in Rockingham County, just to the north of Augusta County, after tracking his cell phone’s location to Harrisonburg.
Troopers first tried to initiate a traffic stop while the 37-year-old was at a rest area off the interstate, but he got back in his vehicle and drove away.
Police followed Grant’s vehicle; he pulled over to the side of the interstate about five miles down the road at the 227-mile marker. According to police, Grant got out of the vehicle with a gun pointed to his head and shot himself at around 10:30 a.m.
Grant, of Charlotte, North Carolina, was pronounced dead at a nearby hospital.
Keen said officers responded at about 7 a.m. to multiple 911 calls reporting an active shooter at the United Rentals facility.
“When officers arrived on the scene, they found three victims on site,” Keen said. “All three were employees of United Rental.”
Two of the wounded employees were taken to Prince William Medical Center, while the third was transported to Inova Fairfax Hospital and is expected to survive. Keen said he knew Lamot personally, and described him as a “deep family man” who coached youth football.
Investigators identified the suspected shooter as Grant, who Keen said was also a “fairly new employee” of United Rentals.
Grant reportedly changed the tags on his silver Toyota Camry overnight and fled the area with temporary North Carolina plates, according to Keen. Police issued an alert for Grant to law enforcement agencies across Virginia and worked with state and federal partners to locate him.
Two of the employees were in the garage area when the shooting happened, Keen said. The third came from an office area into the garage.
Video from inside the United Rentals facility is also being reviewed as part of the investigation. Keen said there were “many shots fired,” though investigators had not yet determined how many.
Police said an autopsy will be performed on the men who were killed and the investigation continues.
The police response initially affected nearby schools. Jennie Dean Elementary School students and staff were redirected to Metz Middle School while police secured the area.
Schools in the area were initially placed on lockdown as a precaution; Keen said those lockdowns have been lifted. According to police, Dean Elementary will be under a secure status until the end of the school day; normal operations may continue, but no one is allowed to enter or exit the school.
Police said Grant has a North Carolina address and investigators are working with United Rentals to determine whether he also has a local address.

Multiple Victims Seriously Injured After Shooting In Manassas, Suspect At Large: Police
Multiple people were left in critical condition after a Wednesday morning shooting in Manassas. Police are still looking for the suspect.

MANASSAS, VA – Three people were seriously injured Wednesday in a shooting in Manassas, and a search is underway for the suspect, according to police.
According to Manassas police, three men were left with life-threatening injuries after they were shot by a coworker at their place of employment, United Rentals, located in the 9400 block of Wellington Road, at about 7 a.m. Wednesday.

Speaking to the press later Wednesday morning, Manassas City Police Chief Douglas Keen said two victims had been transported to Prince William Hospital and the third to a Fairfax hospital.
Keen said police believe a handgun was used in the attack, but the weapon was not found at the scene. Many other employees were at the site at the time of the shooting, he said.
Find out what's happening in Manassasfor free with the latest updates from Patch.
The shooting suspect is Marvin Grant, 37, described as a light-skinned Black man approximately 5 feet 9 inches tall with brown eyes and brown hair. He may be driving a gray Toyota Camry or Toyota Corolla displaying temporary North Carolina registration tags.
Anyone who sees the suspect or vehicle should call 911.
Manassas police say they believe Grant has left the Northern Virginia area, and that they are distributing descriptions of the suspect and vehicle across the state.

Officers found three men, all employees of United Rentals, who had been shot.

Troopers did not use force.

Two of the victims were in the business’s garage or bay area, police said. The third came from an office area and entered the garage. Police are reviewing surveillance video from inside the facility.

sources.news_title: Two Killed in Manassas Shooting; Suspect Dies From Self-Inflicted Gunshot on I-81
sources.text:
MANASSAS, Va. (VR) – On September 30, 2026, at 7:11 a.m., we received a call for a shooting at United Rentals located at 9415 Wellington Rd. 
Officers arrived on scene at 7:14 from both Manassas City Police and the Prince William County Sheriff’s Office.
Officers located three victims and provided emergency medical aid. The offender, identified as Marvin Grant, fled the scene in a silver Toyota Camry before police arrived. All individuals were transported to a local area hospital. Two victims have since died, and one remains hospitalized but is in stable condition. All next of kin have been notified.
Through our investigation, we determined Mr. Grant was an employee of United Rentals. Motive remains unclear at this time. Detectives immediately began a phone ping for the offender’s cell phone. The phone was located in Harrisonburg, Virginia, and information was provided to Virginia State Police.
Deceased Victims: Lamot, Ricky 48 y/o, Serrano, Christopher 33 y/o
From Virginia State Police:
At approximately 8:20 a.m. this morning (Sept. 30, 2026), Virginia State Police were alerted to be on the lookout for Marvin Grant, 37, of Charlotte, N.C., a suspect wanted in a shooting incident in Manassas City earlier this morning, and that Grant may be in Rockingham County.
A Virginia State Police trooper spotted the suspect’s vehicle on Interstate 81 southbound near the 235-mile marker in Augusta County. The suspect vehicle pulled into the rest area at the 232-mile marker, where Virginia State Police troopers attempted a traffic stop. The suspect exited his vehicle, then returned to his vehicle, and continued driving southbound on Interstate 81. Troopers initiated a pursuit in response.
At the 227-mile marker, the suspect pulled over on the side of the interstate and exited the vehicle with a firearm pointed at his head. The Virginia State Police tactical team and a negotiator were brought to the scene. At approximately 10:30 a.m., the suspect suffered a self-inflicted gunshot wound. He was taken to an area hospital where he was pronounced deceased. There was no use of force by Virginia State Police. The incident remains under investigation
Offender: Grant, Marvin 37 y/o Deceased
This is still an active investigation. If you have any information regarding this incident, please contact Detective Speights at 703-257-8041, or Detective Dranko at 703-257-8046.
If you have any questions regarding the Virginia State Police, please contact matthew.demlein@vsp.virginia.gov. Our condolences go out to the victims and their families. This is a traumatic incident that has impacted many within our 
community.
We’d like to thank our partners with the Prince William Sheriff’s Office, Virginia State Police, Manassas Park Police, Prince William County Police, and Manassas City Fire and Rescue for their assistance with this incident. We’d also like to thank the community for their patience while we conduct our investigation.

sources.text:
Three United Rentals employees suffered potentially life-threatening injuries after a colleague allegedly opened fire at the company’s Manassas facility before fleeing, authorities said
Police in Virginia are searching for a man accused of opening fire on coworkers at a United Rentals facility in Manassas, leaving three employees critically injured in what authorities described as an act of workplace violence.
The shooting unfolded at the company’s location in Manassas, a city about 30 miles from Washington, according to local police. Investigators identified the suspected shooter as 37-year-old Marvin Grant, who fled the scene and remained at large.
Manassas Police Chief Douglas Keen said all three victims worked for the same company. Emergency responders transported the wounded employees to a nearby hospital, where they were being treated for gunshot injuries described by authorities as potentially life-threatening.
Police characterized the incident as workplace violence and continued their search for Grant as the investigation moved forward. Officials have not released additional information regarding the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

sources.news_title: Jennie Dean Elementary Secure Status in Manassas, VA
sources.text:
Jennie Dean Elementary School in Manassas, Virginia was placed under a “Secure the Building” status Wednesday after police activity and road closures broke out near the campus, prompting officials to move all students and staff to nearby Metz Middle School. Manassas City Public Schools said all Dean Elementary students and staff are safe and will remain at Metz until further notice.
The disruption hit just weeks after the school reopened in a brand-new $56 million facility at 9601 Prince William Street, according to DC News Now, which reported the incident. That new building, unveiled in early August, was constructed to serve about 900 students in prekindergarten through fourth grade, according to Potomac Local News, with construction beginning in late 2024 next to the original 1960s school building. The school serves students in prekindergarten through fourth grade, underscoring how young the population involved in Wednesday's disruption was.
Manassas City Police restricted access to Wellington Road and the Route 28 bypass as the situation developed, per the same DC News Now report. Manassas City Public Schools announced the restricted access to the campus in a social media post, and the report notes that all Dean Elementary students and staff were being redirected to Metz Middle School, where they were expected to stay until further notice.
What ‘Secure the Building’ Actually Means
The secure status is a specific tier below a full lockdown under the division's Standard Response Protocol. Manassas City Public Schools emergency procedures call for locking exterior doors and restricting outside access while internal activities continue as normal — a distinction from a lockdown, which requires locking interior classrooms and keeping occupants out of sight, according to the school division's own emergency guidance.
Students were relocated to Metz Middle School. The length of the road restrictions remained unclear.
A Campus Built on Historic Ground
The elementary school carries the name of Jennie Serepta Dean, who was born into slavery in 1848 and went on to found the historic Manassas Industrial School for Colored Youth on the same site in 1893, according to City of Manassas historical records. The site continues to serve an educational role as Jennie Dean Elementary School.
A City Already on Edge
Wednesday's incident lands in a Manassas that has seen a string of public safety scares in recent weeks. A 16-year-old was fatally shot during a First Friday community event in Old Town Manassas earlier in September, according to NBC4 Washington, an incident Hoodline covered in gunfire that sent crowds fleeing.
The police response was prompted by a shooting in the 9400 block of Wellington Road, while the length of the road restrictions remained unclear. Manassas City Public Schools has said all Dean Elementary students and staff are safe and are being redirected to Metz Middle School, where they will remain until further notice.
